accuracy.evidence: Matches Y1 Maths measurement: measure and begin to record capacity/volume; non-standard cups plus litres; capacity as how much when full.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets full-now=capacity, taller=more, unequal cups, and missing units in fill/compare/fullnow/tall/challenge why() and adult notes.

lab_distinct.evidence: Lab measures capacity with cup counts and litres — distinct from qualitative full/empty language (flagheavy) and length/height cubes (flaglenht).

lab_teaches.evidence: Learner fills by cups, compares holds-more, records units, rejects full-now, picks short-wide over tall-thin when cups say so.

predictions.evidence: Wrong options (full-now, taller always, no unit, height-only) are overturned by fill/compare/record/fullnow/tall tasks.

challenge_feedback.evidence: why() names now/half/empty, tall/taller/most/wins, random/never/nohelp, doodle/length/leaves slips specifically.

readability.evidence: Ages 5–6 wording: short kid lines; capacity, cups, litres named plainly.

no_filler.evidence: No delve/journey phrasing; each line teaches measuring, recording, or a myth to reject.

mobile.evidence: Large pour/compare buttons; tap twins for drag; challenge stack usable at phone width; young class.

accessibility.evidence: Fill, compare, record, fullnow, tall, idea expose lbtn twins; say() updates canvas aria-label; challenge uses aria-live status.

sources: UK National Curriculum Maths Y1: measure and begin to record capacity and volume
NCETM / White Rose Y1 measurement: capacity with non-standard units; introduce litres
BBC Bitesize KS1 Maths: capacity — how much a container can hold
